title: Closed inverse image preserves limits
statement:
Let $X$ be quasi-compact and quasi-separated, $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ a
closed immersion with quasi-compact open complement, and $B$ a sheaf of rings
on $X_{\mathrm{proét}}$. Then:

1. for every weakly contractible affine $V$ in the affine ind-étale basis of
$Z_{\mathrm{proét}}$ (over an affine open of $X$) and every $B$-module sheaf $F$,
the canonical map $F(v(V))\to(i^*F)(V)$ is an isomorphism, where $v(V)$ is the
henselian lift of [def-exc-closed-site-lift];
2. the functor $i^*$ from $B$-module sheaves on $X_{\mathrm{proét}}$ to
$i^*B$-module sheaves on $Z_{\mathrm{proét}}$ is exact and preserves all small
limits and all small colimits.

external.place: The weakly contractible affines form a basis of $Z_{\mathrm{proét}}$ (Bhatt–Scholze, Proposition 4.2.8), and a morphism of sheaves that is bijective on the objects of a basis is an isomorphism.

proof.text: Let W=v(V) over Spec A. The cartesian affine chart identifies the global closed fibre of W with the image of u(W) under the open-chart inclusion. Transfer weak contractibility across this canonical isomorphism. To prove projective evaluation at u(W) in the local affine basis, lift a section of an epimorphism after one affine surjective cover q. Its image in the global closed site is covering by [lem-weil-pbc-ind-etale-basis] and weakly etale composition. Subcanonical Yoneda [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-subcanonical] makes its representable map epi; global weak contractibility splits q. Full faithfulness of the affine inclusion and of composition along the open immersion gives a local section, so the section lifts without a cover. This is projectiveEvaluation_openChart in Lean. The epi criterion is [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheaf-sets-epi-locally-surjective].

Use the fully faithful lift adjunction of [lem-weil-pbc-affine-closed-site-functor-properties]. On affine-basis sheaves, sheafified precomposition with v is left adjoint to restriction along u. The direct-image square with the full sites commutes. Its inverse mate is invertible by [lem-stage3-inverse-mate-equivalences]. The mate unit equation identifies the actual affine unit at W with the unit of this affine-basis adjunction, up to invertible comparisons. The latter is restriction along the lift counit followed by sheafification at u(W). The counit at W=v(V) is invertible by full faithfulness and the triangle identity. The evaluation argument of [lem-weil-pbc-affine-closed-inverse-image-evaluation], applied to projective u(W), makes the sheafification unit bijective. Sheafification commutes with forgetting abelian groups, so this is an isomorphism of abelian groups. This is affineUnit_from_projectiveFiber, with the set-valued evaluation helpers imported from the existing evaluation module.

Globalize the specific unit, not just an unspecified isomorphism. The chart square induces pullbackMapComparison, invertible because the square is cartesian. Rotating it on the site level gives pullbackComp.inv, pullbackCongr.hom and pullbackComp.hom; equality is checked by the two fibre-product projections. Applying sheaves and the localization adjunctions gives an invertible rotated mate. Mathlib iterated_mateEquiv_conjugateEquiv and conjugateIsoEquiv then make the inverse-image mate invertible. Finally unit_mateEquiv_symm identifies the restricted global unit followed by the direct-image comparison with the local unit followed by the inverse-image comparison. The local unit is invertible by step 2, hence so is the specified global component. The Lean helpers siteMate_eq, isIso_inverseMate_localRestrictionBaseChange and isIso_unit_sections_of_localization contain these calculations. This proves clause (1) for every underlying abelian sheaf F.X.

proof.text: Apply the abelian-sheaf clause of [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-immersion-limit-preservation] to i, which is in particular a locally closed immersion. It gives all small limits for L=i^{-1} on abelian sheaves. No commutative-ring coefficient clause of that theorem is used.

For an arbitrary monoid B in abelian sheaves, limits of B-module objects are created on underlying abelian sheaves: the action on a limit is the unique map whose composites with all projections are the coordinate actions. The module axioms and linearity follow by those projections, as in [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-limits-sectionwise], implemented for this encoding by Mod.createsLimit in WeilConjectures.CategoryTheory.Monoidal.Mod.Limits. Thus Mod.forget preserves limits and reflects isomorphisms and hence limit cones. The underlying functor of L.mapMod B is definitionally Mod.forget B followed by L. Reflecting preservation through the target forgetful functor gives all small module limits.

Use the existing monoidal inverse/direct-image adjunction of [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image] and its mapModAdjunction B to lift it to modules over B and LB. By [lem-weil-pbc-left-adjoint-preserves-colimits] its left adjoint L.mapMod B preserves all small colimits. The finite-limit and finite-colimit assertions follow by specialization of all-small preservation. None of these module-object constructions assumes B commutative.
